Subject: [PATCH] Title-page has page-num 0 again.

This is a fix for a bug

diff --git a/src/net/nightwhistler/pageturner/view/bookview/BookView.java b/src/net/nightwhistler/pageturner/view/bookview/BookView.java
index 44f6f8e..250d088 100644
--- a/src/net/nightwhistler/pageturner/view/bookview/BookView.java
+++ b/src/net/nightwhistler/pageturner/view/bookview/BookView.java
@@ -1080,7 +1080,7 @@ public class BookView extends ScrollView implements LinkTagHandler.LinkCallBack
 
         LOG.debug( "Looking for pageNumber for index=" + index + ", position=" + position );
 		
-		int pageNum = 0;
+		int pageNum = -1;
 		
 		List<List<Integer>> pageOffsets = spine.getPageOffsets();
 		
-- 
2.48.1

## Summary

**File modified:** `src/net/nightwhistler/pageturner/view/bookview/BookView.java`

**Modification:** Changed the initial value of the local variable `pageNum` from `0` to `-1` inside the method that calculates the page number for a given index and position.

**Relationship / Reasoning:**
This is a single, isolated change in one file. The variable `pageNum` is initialized before iterating through `pageOffsets` to determine the page number corresponding to a given index and position. Previously, initializing `pageNum` to `0` caused the title page to always be incorrectly treated as page number `0`, even when no matching offset was found. By changing the default to `-1`, the method now distinguishes between "no page number found" (`-1`) and "found page 0", which restores correct behavior for the title page (allowing it to properly be recognized as page `0` rather than colliding with the default initialization value). This fix ensures the page-numbering logic correctly reflects the actual page index rather than defaulting ambiguously to 0.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`int pageNum = 0;`
`pageNum += pages;`
`for ( int i=0; i < offsets.size() && offsets.get(i) <= position; i++ ) { pageNum++; }`
Reason: `pageNum` is initialized to `0`, which is also a valid page number for the title page. As the loops accumulate offsets and increment `pageNum`, there is no way to distinguish between the initial "no pages counted yet" state and a legitimately computed page number of `0`. When the index/position calculation results in the title page (page 0), this ambiguity causes the final returned `pageNum` to be indistinguishable from the uninitialized starting state, leading to incorrect handling and loss of the correct page number for the title page.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`int pageNum = -1;`
Reason: By initializing `pageNum` to `-1`, an invalid value that can never occur as an actual page number, the code removes the ambiguity between "not yet computed" and "computed page 0". Now, as the loops add to `pageNum` based on offsets found in `pageOffsets`, the final value of `0` can only be reached through legitimate computation (i.e., when the title page truly matches), ensuring the title page is correctly assigned a page number of `0` instead of being conflated with the initial sentinel state.
